requirements.requirement: The system must include a malpractice object in the provider detail API response when malpractice data is available.
The system must ensure the malpractice object conforms to the UI schema defined in EVAL-P-MALPRACTICE-UX-S1.
The system must correctly parse malpractice.status from the API response into the frontend component state without transformation errors.
The system must correctly bind malpractice.score_contribution to the UI display component.
The system must render the malpractice component when the malpractice object is present in the API response.
The system must default malpractice.status to 'unknown' when the malpractice object is missing or null in the API response.
The system must gracefully omit optional fields (case_count, last_incident_date) from rendering when they are null or undefined.
The system must not throw runtime errors when the malpractice object is absent from the API response.
The system must validate that state_board_url, if present, is passed through the API and rendered unchanged in the UI.
The system must complete an end-to-end flow where malpractice data originates from evaluate_care_facade.py and is visible in the frontend UI.
The system must ensure that malformed malpractice data (e.g., invalid status value) results in a fallback to 'unknown' status.
The system must ensure that missing malpractice.score_contribution results in no score contribution displayed rather than an error.
The system must ensure LLM-generated UI text does not introduce prohibited terms such as 'fraud' or 'misconduct' when rendering malpractice data.
The system must ensure LLM-assisted summarization preserves the original malpractice status without reinterpretation or amplification.
The system must ensure LLM output reflects 'unknown' when malpractice data is missing and does not hallucinate case details.
The system must ensure LLM output uses neutral, signal-based language consistent with feature requirements when describing malpractice status.
The system must ensure LLM output does not fabricate state board URLs when none are provided in the API response.
The system must ensure LLM output includes malpractice data only when present in the structured response payload.
